1869| *

1873| *
1874| * [+-]?.[0-9]+(.[0-9]+)?([Ee][+-]?[0-9]+)?

1881| *
1882| *       PNG floating point numbers are not greedy.

joined_facts.statement: The entry accepts fuzzer bytes as a PNG stream. It rejects inputs shorter than eight bytes or with a mismatched signature, then supplies the remaining bytes through user_read_data.

The harness sets both CRC actions to PNG_CRC_QUIET_USE and conditionally enables PNG_IGNORE_ADLER32 when that macro exists.

joined_facts.statement: If the supplied bytes end before a requested read length, the harness callback calls png_error. The harness has setjmp cleanup paths around reading and row processing.
The complete old harness contains no explicit assert invocation. Its existing checks include signature, allocation, IHDR, dimension and setjmp error gates.
The target is a C++ fuzz entry linked against the libpng static library and zlib.
The supplied recipe edits pnglibconf.dfa to disable STDIO, WARNING, and WRITE, then runs autoreconf, configure, and the library build. It supplies no additional configure option in these lines.
Inputs shorter than eight bytes or failing the PNG signature check return before libpng read object creation; the remaining bytes become the read callback's buffer.
The read callback copies requested bytes from BufState, advances its pointer and remaining count, and calls png_error if the request exceeds the remaining input.
The target sets quiet-use CRC handling for critical and ancillary chunks and enables PNG_IGNORE_ADLER32 only when that macro is defined.
The primary read sequence creates read and info objects, installs the buffer callback, marks eight signature bytes consumed, then calls png_read_info and png_read_update_info.

After updating info, the target allocates one row using png_get_rowbytes, obtains IHDR values, rejects dimensions whose product exceeds 100000000, sets interlace handling, reads each row for every pass, and calls png_read_end.
The target has setjmp recovery around reading and row processing; each recovery path invokes PNG_CLEANUP and returns zero.
PNG_CLEANUP frees the row, destroys the read structures, and nulls their pointers. The handler destructor also destroys remaining objects and deletes BufState.
The supplied source exposes read chunk handlers for iCCP, zTXt, and iTXt only under their respective PNG_READ_*_SUPPORTED gates.
ICC colorspace acceptance requires valid length, header, and tag table checks and returns zero when the colorspace is already invalid or any check fails.

An invalid colorspace clears the iCCP information flag and frees its profile. png_get_iCCP returns profile data only when that flag is set and all required output pointers are supplied; rejection of an invalid profile therefore does not itself establish loss of a supported accepted-profile behavior.

The supplied png_set_benign_errors implementation says its default treats png_benign_error as an error; passing a nonzero allowed value sets the benign-error and application-warning/error warning flags.
The read structure includes user chunk and decompressed-allocation limits when PNG_USER_LIMITS_SUPPORTED is enabled; the comments specify that zero means unlimited for each.

The complete target entry contains no explicit assert invocation or comparison of decoded output; its existing checks are the input gates, object-creation checks, setjmp recovery, IHDR availability check, and dimension limit.
The entry reads a PNG from fuzz input through image rows and calls png_read_end with a separate end_info_ptr. Post-IDAT metadata is within the requested read-to-end operation.

The entry requires at least eight input bytes with a PNG signature and rejects images when width × height exceeds 100,000,000; its callback consumes the remaining input bytes and reports an overread through png_error.
